Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

language noun

also tongue, mother tongue, foreign language

classical

Caes. BG 1.1: quī ipsōrum linguā Celtae, nostrā Gallī appellantur
Cic. Fin. 1.10: Latīnam linguam nōn modo nōn inopem … sed locuplētiōrem etiam esse quam Graecam
Traupman 337

lingua, linguae f.

noun, first declension

language, tongue

Utraque lingua, both languages: for a Roman, Greek and Latin (Hor. S. 1.10.23; Quint. 1.1.14).

Other words

  • sermō, sermōnis m. — language, the speech of a people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.12: ā sermōne Graecō puerum incipere mālō; Cic. de Or. 3.42 (Lewis & Short): in Latīnō sermōne; Traupman 337

    Sermō Latīnus, the Latin language; also talk, conversation (see talk).

  • idiōma, idiōmatis n. — a language

    noun, third declension · also used · medieval · M-O s.v. language; Charis. (Lewis & Short): an idiom

    In late antiquity a turn of phrase peculiar to a language (Charisius); a language only in medieval and later Latin (Dante, Marco Polo, in Morgan–Owens). Classical prose says lingua or sermō.

Examples

  • tertiam quī ipsōrum linguā Celtae, nostrā Gallī appellantur

    the third by those who are called Celts in their own language, Gauls in oursCaes. BG 1.1

  • ita fīet, ut, cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus, neutra alterī officiat

    So it will come about that, once we begin to look after both languages with equal care, neither will get in the other’s way.Quint. 1.1.14

  • vel Mithridātēs, cui duās et vīgintī linguās, quot nātiōnibus imperābat, trāditur nōtās fuisse

    or Mithridates, who is said to have known twenty-two languages, one for each nation he ruledQuint. 11.2.50

See also speak, word, in English, in Bulgarian, in Portuguese, programming language.
